- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to avoid undershoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop; add 2–5% downward bias to forecast to reflect sentiment-driven volatility.
- Model frequently underestimates long-term (30d) declines when sentiment is negative; apply a 3–5% downward adjustment to the first 10 days of forecast if sentiment <0.4.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings >0.2), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment momentum, especially if sentiment is trending upward.
- If model forecast is >15% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–10% if sentiment is weak or neutral; if sentiment is strong, allow slight overshoot but cap at +10%.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (first 5 days), model often misses it; adjust first 5 days downward by 3–7% if sentiment is negative or uncertain.
